subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Small cell lung cancer: staging classification, chemoimmunotherapy, thoracic irradiation and prophylactic cranial irradiation

steps.tx: Small cell lung cancer SCLC is clinically staged using the Veterans Administration Lung Cancer Study Group classification into limited-stage and extensive-stage disease. **Limited-stage SCLC** is defined as disease anatomically confined to the ipsilateral hemithorax, mediastinum, and supraclavicular nodes that can be safely encompassed within a tolerable single radiation therapy field. Conversely, extensive-stage disease produces distant metastases, malignant pleural effusions, or contralateral hilar adenopathy.

left.title: Limited-Stage SCLC (LS-SCLC)
points: Confined to one hemithorax and regional nodes
Encompassed within a single radiation port

steps.tx: For limited-stage disease, the established standard of care comprises concurrent **accelerated hyperfractionated** thoracic radiation paired with 4 cycles of cisplatin and etoposide. Thoracic radiation delivers 45 Gy across 30 twice-daily fractions of 150 cGy over 3 weeks, beginning early during cycle 1 or 2 of chemotherapy. Accelerated delivery counters rapid neuroendocrine tumour cell repopulation, providing superior long-term local control and overall survival over once-daily radiation.

steps.tx: In newly diagnosed **extensive-stage SCLC**, front-line systemic therapy requires combining platinum and etoposide with **PD-L1 inhibitors** such as atezolizumab or durvalumab. Landmark phase III trials IMpower133 with **atezolizumab** and CASPIAN with **durvalumab** demonstrated statistically significant improvements in overall survival over chemotherapy alone. Chemoimmunotherapy for 4 cycles followed by maintenance PD-L1 inhibitor monotherapy represents the universal standard of care.

steps.tx: In limited-stage small cell lung cancer, the landmark **ADRIATIC trial** established a major survival paradigm shift. Patients with limited-stage disease without progression after definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy received consolidation **durvalumab** for up to 2 years. Durvalumab consolidation demonstrated dramatic, statistically significant improvements in both progression-free survival and overall survival, establishing consolidation immunotherapy in curative-intent limited SCLC.

steps.tx: Because small cell lung cancer exhibits high neurotropism, **Prophylactic cranial irradiation** PCI to 25 Gy in 10 fractions significantly reduces brain metastasis incidence and improves overall survival. In limited-stage patients achieving complete or good partial response, PCI reduces symptomatic brain relapse by more than 50%. In extensive-stage disease, serial surveillance brain MRI provides an evidence-based alternative to upfront PCI to avoid neurocognitive decline.

left.title: PCI Indications & Benefits
points: Indicated in LS-SCLC after good response to CRT
Reduces cumulative brain metastases from 60% to 30%
Standard dose: 25 Gy in 10 daily fractions

right.title: Neurocognitive Risks & Alternatives
points: Delayed cognitive slowing and memory decline
MRI surveillance every 3 months in extensive-stage

steps.tx: Bispecific antibody **Tarlatamab** represents an innovative DLL3-directed **bispecific T-cell engager** BiTE approved for pretreated extensive-stage SCLC. Delta-like ligand 3 DLL3 is aberrantly expressed on the cell surface of over 85% of small cell lung cancers while absent on normal adult tissues. By crosslinking DLL3 on tumour cells with CD3 on cytotoxic T cells, tarlatamab induces targeted perforin-mediated neuroendocrine tumour cell lysis.

steps.tx: Synthetic tetrahydronaphthyridine alkaloid **Lurbinectedin** selectively binds DNA minor groove guanine residues, bending DNA and inhibiting **RNA polymerase II** elongation during active oncogenic transcription. Lurbinectedin is approved for second-line extensive-stage SCLC progressing after front-line platinum chemotherapy. In addition to direct tumour cell apoptosis, lurbinectedin inhibits tumour-associated macrophages, suppressing vascular endothelial growth factor production in the tumour microenvironment.

rows: Selective RNA polymerase II and transcription inhibitor
Topoisomerase I inhibitor; DNA single-strand breaks
Grade 4 neutropenia; active in refractory disease

steps.tx: Small cell lung cancer produces severe paraneoplastic neurological and endocrine syndromes due to aberrant neuroendocrine polypeptide secretion. The **syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone** SIADH presents with euvolemic hyponatraemia driven by ectopic vasopressin, treated with fluid restriction and vasopressin V2-receptor antagonists. In contrast, **Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome** results from autoantibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels, causing proximal muscle weakness that improves with exercise.

left.title: SIADH Paraneoplastic
points: Urine sodium > 30 mEq/L with concentrated urine
Treated with fluid restriction or tolvaptan

right.title: Lambert-Eaton (LEMS)
points: Proximal leg weakness and autonomic dysfunction
